Pair JSON stores {"tag": ..., "content": string, "children": [...]}.
The content key is omitted when the node has no content_span.
External source spans are optional and omitted from JSON. Content is required
where the node owns spelling (including calls and named declarations).
All examples below omit trivia; semantic slot indexes exclude comments.

$a
=> Var("a")[]

.a.b.c
=> Path[String[StringChunk("a")], String[StringChunk("b")], String[StringChunk("c")]]

.a[2:3]
=> Path[`"a"`, Slice[Int(2), Int(3)]]

.a[:3]
=> Path[`"a"`, Slice[Int(0), Int(3)]]

.a[$start:]
=> Path[`"a"`, Slice[Var("start")]]

$a.b.c
=> Invoke(".")[Var("a"), Path[`"b"`, `"c"`]]

..
=> Invoke("..")[]

$__loc__
=> Loc[StringChunk(FILE), Int(LINE)]

.a as $x | $x
=> Bind[`.a`, Var("x"), Var("x")]

. as {$x} ?// [$x] | $x
=> Bind[Path[], Var("x"), Object[`"x"`, Var("x")], Array[Var("x")]]

def f(x; $y): x + $y; f(1; 2)
=> Def("f")[Invoke("x")[], Var("y"), Invoke("+")[Invoke("x")[], Var("y")], Invoke("f")[Int(1), Int(2)]]

a | b | c
=> Invoke("|")[Invoke("a")[], Invoke("b")[], Invoke("c")[]]

{"a": 20, "b": t | c}
=> Object[`"a"`, Int(20), `"b"`, Invoke("|")[Invoke("t")[], Invoke("c")[]]]

Only explicitly neutral singleton pipe/comma containers collapse. Never remove
f(.), -f, try f, or f? based solely on their argument count. Parentheses are
reconstructed from operation precedence, associativity, and syntactic context.
Comments are childless trivia; pretty output preserves them and inline/compact
output drops them. Source positions are not used to recover missing semantics.

reduce .[] as {$x} ?// [$x] (0; . + $x)
=> Reduce[EXPR, INIT, UPDATE, Object[`"x"`, Var("x")], Array[Var("x")]]

foreach .[] as $x (0; . + $x; . * 2)
=> ForEach[EXPR, INIT, UPDATE, EXTRACT, Var("x")]
